main.title: Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII
main.subtitle: Lightning faces the final days of her world
main.summary: Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII is a 2013 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix.

cards.heading: A new battle system and a world running out of time
cards.text: Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy XIII is a 2013 action role-playing game developed and published by Square Enix. A sequel to Final Fantasy XIII-2, it concludes the storyline of Final Fantasy XIII and forms part of the Fabula Nova Crystallis subseries. It was released in 2013 in Japan and 2014 in North America and the PAL regions. It was ported to Windows in 2015 and Android and iOS via cloud gaming in 2016 in Japan. Lightning Returns employs a highly revamped version of the gameplay system from the previous two games, with an action-oriented battle system, the ability to customize the player character's outfits, and a time limit the player must extend by completing story missions and side quests.

cards.heading: Lightning’s mission before the end
cards.text: The game takes place five hundred years after the previous game's ending. Lightning, the main protagonist of the first game and a key character in the second, awakes from a self-imposed hibernation thirteen days before the world's end. The deity Bhunivelze chooses her to save the people of the dying world, including former friends and allies who have developed heavy emotional burdens. As she travels, she learns the truth behind the world's fate and Bhunivelze's true agenda.

cards.heading: Development and the conclusion of the XIII storyline
cards.text: The game's development began in May 2012, shortly after the release of the last DLC for XIII-2, and it was revealed in September of that year as part of the Final Fantasy 25th Anniversary Event. The key creative minds and developers from the preceding games returned, and Square Enix's First Production Department created it, with tri-Ace assisting with graphics development. The development team wanted the game to conclude the story of Lightning and the XIII universe, as well as address criticisms leveled at the previous two games.

cards.heading: Sales and critical reception
cards.text: The game sold 277,000 units in its first week of release in Japan and went on to become the 17th best-selling game of the year, selling over 400,000 copies by the end of 2013. As of May 2014, 800,000 copies have been sold. Critics have given the game mixed reviews: while they mainly praised the game's battle system, opinions on the graphics, time limit, and other aspects of gameplay were varied, and the story and characters were criticized for being weak or poorly developed.

main.title: Super Mario 3D World
main.subtitle: Mario and his friends enter the Sprixie Kingdom
main.summary: Super Mario 3D World is a 2013 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii U.

cards.heading: A new 3D platform game for Wii U
cards.text: Super Mario 3D World is a 2013 platform game developed and published by Nintendo for the Wii U. It is the sixth original 3D platform game in the Super Mario series and the sequel to Super Mario 3D Land (2011). The game was re-released for the Nintendo Switch as Super Mario 3D World + Bowser's Fury in February 2021.

cards.heading: The Sprixie Kingdom and the Cat transformation
cards.text: Players control Mario and his friends as they attempt to rescue fairy-like creatures called Sprixies from Bowser, who invades the realm known as the Sprixie Kingdom. Gameplay is similar to previous Mario games, with players progressing through levels to reach Bowser. It features a character selector as well as introducing a power-up called the Super Bell, which turns the player into a cat, enabling them to climb walls and use a scratch attack.

cards.heading: Critical reception, sales and the Captain Toad spinoff
cards.text: Super Mario 3D World was acclaimed for its level design, presentation, replay value, and soundtrack, though some reviewers criticized its unreliable camera in the multiplayer mode. The game was a commercial success, with the Wii U version selling 5.89 million units and the Nintendo Switch version selling 13.47 million units worldwide as of March 2024, becoming the second best-selling game for Wii U and one of the best-selling games for Nintendo Switch. Between both versions, a total of 19.36 million units have been sold worldwide. A spinoff game, Captain Toad: Treasure Tracker, was released in November 2014.

main.title: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds
main.subtitle: Link moves through walls between Hyrule and Lorule
main.summary: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds is a 2013 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS.

cards.heading: A spiritual successor to A Link to the Past
cards.text: The Legend of Zelda: A Link Between Worlds is a 2013 action-adventure game developed and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS. The game is the 17th in The Legend of Zelda series and is a spiritual successor to the 1991 title The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past. Announced in April 2013, A Link Between Worlds was released in Australia, Europe, and North America in November, and in Japan a month later.

cards.heading: A bracelet turns Link into a painting
cards.text: The story is set many years after the events of A Link to the Past. Players assume the role of Link, who sets out to restore peace to the kingdom of Hyrule after the evil sorcerer Yuga captures Princess Zelda and escapes through a rift into the parallel world of Lorule. Yuga desires to kidnap the Seven Sages and use their power to resurrect the demon king Ganon. Shortly into his adventure, Link obtains a magic bracelet that grants him the ability to merge into walls as a 2D painting, which allows him to reach new areas and travel between the worlds of Hyrule and Lorule.

cards.heading: Development and the item rental system
cards.text: Concept development began with a small team in 2009, shortly following the completion of Spirit Tracks. During this phase, the game mechanic of Link merging onto walls was prototyped. However, development suffered several setbacks and ceased entirely in late 2010 as core team members were reassigned to different projects. Development restarted in 2011 and the game entered full production in 2012. At the request of series creator Shigeru Miyamoto, the game's world and setting were based on A Link to the Past, though with many of the areas significantly reworked. The game's designers sought to rethink the established conventions of the series, leading to two key changes in the game's structure: allowing players to clear the majority of dungeons in any order they choose, and the introduction of the item rental system.

cards.heading: Critical reception, sales and Tri Force Heroes
cards.text: A Link Between Worlds received critical acclaim, with praise towards its soundtrack, engaging gameplay and new features, and nostalgic feeling, though the art style received mixed reviews. The game also received multiple awards and nominations. It sold over 2.5 million copies worldwide in its first five months, and over 4.26 million copies worldwide by 2022. It received a direct sequel, Tri Force Heroes, in October 2015.

main.title: Forza Motorsport 5
main.subtitle: Turn 10 brings Forza to the Xbox One launch
main.summary: Forza Motorsport 5 is a 2013 racing video game developed by Turn 10 Studios and published by Microsoft Studios for Xbox One.

cards.heading: A launch title with the voices of Top Gear
cards.text: Forza Motorsport 5 is a 2013 racing video game developed by Turn 10 Studios and published by Microsoft Studios for Xbox One. It is the fifth Forza Motorsport and sixth overall installment in the Forza series. The game was revealed on May 21, 2013 during the Xbox One reveal event and was released on November 22, 2013 as a launch title. Jeremy Clarkson, who was featured in the previous installment, Forza Motorsport 4, returned to narrate alongside James May and Richard Hammond, who co-presented alongside Clarkson in Top Gear. The narration was used for the game's commentary when choosing a new event, championship, or league.

cards.heading: Visuals and artificial intelligence praised, content criticized
cards.text: Forza Motorsport 5 received generally positive reviews, with aggregate review websites GameRankings and Metacritic giving a score of 79.49% and 79 out of 100, respectively. Reviewers praised the game's visuals and artificial intelligence, but were critical of the lack of content in relation to its predecessor, Forza Motorsport 4.

main.title: Xbox One
main.subtitle: Games and entertainment share the living room
main.summary: Microsoft presented Xbox One as a shared home-entertainment hub, placing games beside television, communication and the Kinect sensor.

cards.heading: A proposal for the whole living room
cards.text: Xbox One arrived on 22 November 2013 in 13 initial markets. Microsoft presented it as a machine for more than games: television, streaming, Skype and voice control were part of the same living-room proposal. The original large black console and Kinect sensor gave that ambition a physical form.

cards.heading: Games and the sharing of play
cards.text: The games still had to establish what this new Xbox felt like to play. Forza Motorsport 5 focused on cars and circuits, Dead Rising 3 filled its setting with zombies, and Ryse: Son of Rome pursued a cinematic historical spectacle. Around them, features such as Game DVR and Upload made recording and circulating play part of the platform's everyday activity.

cards.heading: The original 2013 model
cards.text: The original large black model preceded the smaller Xbox One S and more powerful One X. With television, streaming, communication and games sharing its interface, the 2013 console reflected Microsoft?s broad ambitions for the living room.

main.title: Gran Turismo 6
main.subtitle: The final Gran Turismo of the PlayStation 3 generation
main.summary: Gran Turismo 6 is a 2013 racing simulation video game developed by Polyphony Digital and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3.

cards.heading: New cars, circuits and partnerships
cards.text: Gran Turismo 6 is a 2013 racing simulation video game developed by Polyphony Digital and published by Sony Computer Entertainment for the PlayStation 3. It is the sixth main installment and the eleventh overall in the Gran Turismo series. The game was released worldwide on December 6, 2013. Gran Turismo 6 received a positive reception and was a financial success. New features included the addition of more cars and tracks, improvements to the car customization options, and partnerships with the Goodwood Festival of Speed, the Ayrton Senna Institute, the FIA, and NASCAR. Gran Turismo 6 is the first game to feature officially FIA-certified content.

cards.heading: From development to the Silverstone announcement
cards.text: Polyphony Digital kept Gran Turismo 6 on PlayStation 3 even as Sony prepared to launch its next console. Announced at Silverstone in May 2013, it promised 1,200 cars and 71 layouts across 33 tracks, with revised physics, adaptive tessellation and a faster interface. Mount Panorama became the series' first Australian circuit. Players could try the new handling through the GT Academy 2013 download.

cards.heading: The Goodwood Festival of Speed enters the game
cards.text: The Goodwood Festival of Speed added a different kind of time trial: a 1.16-mile hill climb through the grounds of the Earl of March's estate. Its narrow course and varied field suited Gran Turismo's mix of everyday cars, rare classics and racing machinery. A festival demonstration let visitors challenge Nick Heidfeld's 1999 record of 41.6 seconds.

cards.heading: Final additions and the launch in Ronda
cards.text: Brands Hatch joined the circuit list, while the fictional Apricot Hill returned after its absence from Gran Turismo 5. New vehicles ranged from the Pagani Huayra and Audi R18 to the Apollo 15 Lunar Roving Vehicle. The Nissan DeltaWing survived a late licensing dispute and appeared in both its 2012 and 2013 forms. December's launch celebration took place in Ronda and at the nearby Ascari circuit in Spain.

main.title: Drakengard 3
main.subtitle: A singer sets out to kill her sisters
main.summary: Drakengard 3 is Access Games' PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 19 December 2013. Zero, an Intoner whose song carries magical power, travels with the dragon Mikhail to kill the five sisters ruling the world's regions. The campaign gradually changes the meaning of that apparent rampage, withholding the reasons behind her actions until the player has spent time within its violence and strange humour. Ground battles and dragon encounters continue the series' structure, while the central relationship brings an unexpectedly childish companion beside a protagonist whose behaviour is difficult to trust.

cards.heading: A singer sets out to kill her sisters
cards.text: Drakengard 3 is Access Games' PlayStation 3 action role-playing game, first released in Japan on 19 December 2013. Zero, an Intoner whose song carries magical power, travels with the dragon Mikhail to kill the five sisters ruling the world's regions. The campaign gradually changes the meaning of that apparent rampage, withholding the reasons behind her actions until the player has spent time within its violence and strange humour. Ground battles and dragon encounters continue the series' structure, while the central relationship brings an unexpectedly childish companion beside a protagonist whose behaviour is difficult to trust.

cards.heading: Change weapons without leaving the fight
cards.text: Zero attacks groups of enemies with several weapon types, each offering a different range and rhythm. Switching between them during combat allows the player to alter an approach without pausing the action. Successful attacks build the Tension Gauge, which enables a temporary Intoner state with greater speed, damage and protection. The player decides when that advantage is worth using, then returns to ordinary fighting once it ends. Dragon sections place Mikhail in the centre of another scale of encounter, connecting the series' ground-based violence to its aerial identity.

cards.heading: A familiar creative team takes another route
cards.text: Yoko Taro returned alongside producer Takamasa Shiba and writer Sawako Natori, with Keisuke Mori also directing at Access Games. The score, led by Keiichi Okabe, connects the production to the team behind Nier while supporting a very different cast and tone. Western editions arrived in May 2014. Reviews welcomed parts of the story and ground combat while criticising technical performance and other elements. Drakengard 3 remains distinctive for the gap between the action first presented and the motives later revealed, asking the player to reconsider a journey already carried out.

main.title: Kirby: Triple Deluxe
main.subtitle: Explore layered stages and inhale giant obstacles with Hypernova
main.summary: Kirby: Triple Deluxe is a 2014 platform game developed by HAL Laboratory and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS. It is the tenth main installment of the Kirby series. The game was released in Japan on January 11, 2014, and in other regions in May. The game follows Kirby as he embarks on a journey through six worlds to rescue King Dedede from Taranza.

cards.heading: Kirby climbs toward the kidnapped King Dedede
cards.text: Kirby: Triple Deluxe is a 2014 platform game developed by HAL Laboratory and published by Nintendo for the Nintendo 3DS. It is the tenth main installment of the Kirby series. The game was released in Japan on January 11, 2014, and in other regions in May. The game follows Kirby as he embarks on a journey through six worlds to rescue King Dedede from Taranza.

cards.heading: Hypernova opens new routes through layered stages
cards.text: Kirby: Triple Deluxe is a platformer displayed in a 2.5D perspective. Some enemy attacks also emanate from the background. Kirby can eat a rainbow-colored Miracle Fruit to become Hypernova Kirby, which allows him to inhale extremely large objects. Bandana Waddle Dee also throws Assist Stars at Kirby, which, by pressing Ⓨ, can heal Kirby.

cards.heading: Four new Copy Abilities join returning powers
cards.text: New copy abilities include Beetle, which allows Kirby to use a Japanese rhinoceros beetle's horn to impale enemies, slam them on the ground, or carry them around; Bell, which lets Kirby wield twin bells, use them as a shield, and attack with sound waves; Archer, which lets Kirby fire arrows and use fake trees and boulders to avoid enemy attacks; and Circus, which allows Kirby to ride on a giant rolling ball to bowl over enemies, juggle flaming bowling pins to attack enemies above him and use exploding balloon animals as weapons. At least 20 copy abilities from previous games return, including Wheel, which was absent from Kirby's Return to Dream Land.

main.title: Nidhogg
main.subtitle: Sword duels and a race across the arena
main.summary: Nidhogg is a side-scrolling two-player fighting video game developed and published by Messhof. Players duel with swords in a pixelated environment. The game was commissioned for the New York University Game Center's annual multiplayer show, and was revised and demoed at private events over the next four years before its final release. It won Indiecade 2013's Game Design award and the 2011 Independent Games Festival's Nuovo Award. It was released for Microsoft Windows on January 13, 2014, and later ported to OS X, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation Vita. Critics praised the feel of the gameplay and its balance, but considered its single-player mode unsatisfying. Messhof released a sequel in 2017 with a higher resolution art style and additional weapons and arenas.

cards.heading: Fencing becomes a competitive tug-of-war
cards.text: Nidhogg is Messhof's 2014 fencing game, in which two opponents fight for the chance to run towards opposite ends of an arena. A kill opens a brief route forward while the defeated player returns to block the way. Commissioned for a New York University Game Center multiplayer show, the game developed through four years of event appearances before its Windows release. Versions for Mac, PlayStation 4 and PlayStation Vita followed.

cards.heading: Movement, sword positions and the final sprint
cards.text: A sword can be held low, in the middle or high. Moving it against the opponent's blade can disarm them, while throwing it trades a ranged attack for the risk of fighting unarmed. Running, jumping, sliding and climbing make a duel part of a larger chase across the level. Reaching the far end wins the match and delivers the winner to the serpent Níðhöggr. Four arenas support local and online duels, with tournament play and variants such as returning boomerang swords.

cards.heading: A strong multiplayer reception
cards.text: Nidhogg received "generally favorable" reviews, according to video game review score aggregator Metacritic. Reviewers praised the feel of the gameplay and its balance, and thought the single-player mode to be unsatisfying. Some critics found technical issues with the online multiplayer code, while others only had issues finding other players.

main.title: Broken Age
main.subtitle: Two stories and a landmark crowdfunding campaign
main.summary: Broken Age is a point-and-click adventure video game developed and published by Double Fine.

cards.heading: Two acts mark Tim Schafer’s return to adventure games
cards.text: Broken Age is a point-and-click adventure developed and published by Double Fine, directed by Tim Schafer. It marked his return to the genre after Grim Fandango in 1998. The game follows two playable characters in separate worlds, with the player able to switch between them. Its release was divided into two acts: the first reached computer players in January 2014, followed by the second in April 2015. Later editions brought the complete adventure to further platforms.

cards.heading: Two protagonists and traditional adventure puzzles
cards.text: The player moves each character through illustrated scenes, examines objects and speaks to the people they meet. Switching protagonists offers another set of places and problems to explore while progress in each story is preserved. Objects go into separate inventories, where they can be combined or dragged onto a suitable part of the scene. Context-sensitive actions keep attention on a possible connection between an object and its surroundings, without requiring the player to select a verb from a separate list.

cards.heading: A Kickstarter campaign changes the funding model
cards.text: Double Fine announced the project as Double Fine Adventure on Kickstarter in February 2012. The initial request was for $400,000 to cover development and a documentary; more than 87,000 backers eventually contributed over $3.45 million. The scale of the response made the campaign an important example of players financing an adventure directly. 2 Player Productions filmed development for an episodic documentary, giving backers a continuing view of the work their contributions supported.
